concepts.label: PAR
concepts.definition: Photosynthetically active radiation, often abbreviated PAR, designates the spectral range (wave band) of solar radiation from 400 to 700 nanometers that photosynthetic organisms are able to use in the process of photosynthesis. This spectral region corresponds more or less with the range of light…

concepts.label: snow
concepts.definition: Snow is an environmental material which is primarily composed of flakes of crystalline water ice. [database_cross_reference: Wikipedia:Snow]

concepts.label: infrared
concepts.definition: Infrared (IR) is invisible radiant energy, electromagnetic radiation with longer wavelengths than those of visible light, extending from the nominal red edge of the visible spectrum at 700 nanometers (frequency 430 THz) to 1 mm (300 GHz).

concepts.label: ultraviolet
concepts.definition: Ultraviolet (UV) light is an electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength from 10 nm (30 PHz) to 380 nm (750 THz), shorter than that of visible light but longer than X-rays. UV radiation is present in sunlight.

concepts.label: Carbon Cycle Component
concepts.definition: The parts that make up the combined processes that cycle carbon, (including photosynthesis, decomposition, and respiration) between its major reservoirs (the atmosphere, oceans, and living organisms).

concepts.label: Dissolved Organic Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The rate at which a mass of dissolved organic carbon moves to or from a particular component of an ecosystem per unit time. Dissolved organic cabon is defined as the fraction of organic matter which is neither excluded nor adsorbed by the filter used to remove particulate organic carbon, and which…

concepts.label: Fire Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon released from burning vegetation per unit time.

concepts.label: Net Ecosystem Exchange Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The magnitude of carbon sources and sinks is defined as the vertical exchange of CO2 between the surface (land or ocean) and the atmosphere.

concepts.label: Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The process of carbon fixation by autotrophic carbon-fixing tissues per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Respiration Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: CO2 produced by organisms and emitted to the environment per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Autotrophic Respiration Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The sum of respiration (CO2 production) by all living parts of primary producers per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Heterotrophic Respiration Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The respiration rate of heterotrophic organisms (animals and microbes) summed per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Gross Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The sum of gross carbon fixation by autotrophic carbon-fixing tissues per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Net Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: Gross primary production (GPP) minus autotrophic respiration (AR) per unit ground or water area and time.

concepts.label: Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A reservoir pool with the capacity to store and release carbon, such as soil, terrestrial vegetation, the ocean, and the atmosphere.

concepts.label: Soil Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained within the top layer of the earth's surface in which plants can grow, consisting of rock and mineral particles mixed with decaying organic matter and having the capability of retaining water.

concepts.label: Plankton Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained in free-floating organisms of the sea and fresh water that for the most part move passively with the water currents and consist mostly of microorganisms and small plants and animals.

concepts.label: Leaf Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained within flattened photosynthetic structures emerging laterally from a main axis or stem and possessing true vascular tissue.

concepts.label: Benthic Algae Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon present in algae on the seafloor.

concepts.label: Grass Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained within monocotyledonous plants of the family Poaceae, having jointed stems sheathed by long, narrow leaves, flowers in spikes, and seedlike fruits.

concepts.label: Wood Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained in the tough, fibrous substance lying beneath the bark of trees and shrubs, consisting of the vascular tissue known as xylem and composed chiefly of cellulose and lignin.

concepts.label: Leaf Litter Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: The mass of carbon contained in the partly decomposed remains of plants on the surface and in the upper layers of the soil.

concepts.label: Dissolved Organic Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A system that has the capacity to store or release carbon, in the form of the organic matter that is able to pass through a filter (filters generally range in size between 0.7 and 0.22 um)

concepts.label: Annual Net Primary Productivity Flux
concepts.definition: Gross primary production (GPP) minus autotrophic respiration (AR) over one year.

concepts.label: Total_Living_Biomass_MOV
concepts.definition: Total carbon content of the living biomass (leaves+roots+wood)

concepts.label: Net_Longwave_Radiation_MOV
concepts.definition: Incident longwave radiation minus simulated outgoing longwave radiation (positive into grnd)

concepts.label: Total_Soil_Wetness_MOV
concepts.definition: Vertically integrated soil moisture divided by maximum allowable soil moisture above wilting point

concepts.label: Near_Surface_CO2_Concentration_MOV
synonyms: Near Surface Carbon Dioxide Concentration MOV
concepts.definition: Near surface dry air CO2 mole fraction (micromoles per mole)

concepts.label: Total_Respiration_MOV
concepts.definition: Total respiration (TotalResp=AutoResp+heteroResp, always positive)

concepts.label: Absorbed_Fraction_Incoming_PAR_MOV
concepts.definition: Absorbed fraction incoming photosyntetically active radiation

concepts.label: Near_Surface_Air_Temperature_MOV
concepts.definition: Near surface air temperature

concepts.label: Leaf_Area_Index_MOV
concepts.definition: Area of leaves per area ground

concepts.label: Surface_Pressure_MOV
concepts.definition: Surface pressure

concepts.label: Average_Layer_Soil_Moisture_MOV
concepts.definition: Soil water content in each soil layer, including liquid, vapor and ice

concepts.label: Average_Layer_Soil_Temperature_MOV
concepts.definition: Average soil temperature in each soil layer

concepts.label: Surface_Runoff_MOV
concepts.definition: Runoff from the landsurface and/or subsurface stormflow

concepts.label: Soil_Layer_Top_Depth_MOV
concepts.definition: Depth from soil surface to top of soil layer

concepts.label: Near_Surface_Module_Of_The_Wind_MOV
synonyms: Near Surface Module of the Wind MOV
concepts.definition: Near surface wind magnitude

concepts.label: Size_Of_Each_Carbon_Pool_MOV
synonyms: Size of Each Carbon Pool MOV
concepts.definition: Total size of each carbon pool vertically integrated over the entire soil column

concepts.label: Soil_Layer_Node_Depth_MOV
concepts.definition: Depth from soil surface to layer prognostic variables; typically center of soil layer

concepts.label: Snow_Water_Equivalent_MOV
concepts.definition: Total water mass of snow pack, including ice and liquid water

concepts.label: Total_Soil_Carbon_MOV
concepts.definition: Total soil and litter carbon content vertically integrated over the enire soil column

concepts.label: Autotrophic_Respiration_MOV
concepts.definition: Autotrophic respiration rate (always positive)

concepts.label: Rainfall_Rate_MOV
concepts.definition: Rainfall rate

concepts.label: Longwave_Albedo_MOV
concepts.definition: Longwave Albedo

concepts.label: Gross_Primary_Productivity_MOV
concepts.definition: MsTMIP Output: Rate of photosynthesis (always positive)

concepts.label: Name_Of_Each_Carbon_Pool_MOV
synonyms: Name of Each Carbon Pool MOV
concepts.definition: Name of each carbon pool (i.e., "wood," or "Coarse Woody Debris")

concepts.label: Soil_Layer_Bottom_Depth_MOV
concepts.definition: Depth from soil surface to bottom of soil layer

concepts.label: Heterotrophic_Respiration_MOV
concepts.definition: Heterotrophic respiration rate (always positive)

concepts.label: Active_Layer_Thickness_MOV
concepts.definition: Thaw depth; depth to zero centigrade isotherm in permafrost

concepts.label: Net_Shortwave_Radiation_MOV
concepts.definition: Incident shortwave radiation minus simulated outgoing shortwave radiation (positive into grnd)

concepts.label: Total_Snow_Depth_MOV
concepts.definition: Total snow depth

concepts.label: Fire_Emissions_MOV
concepts.definition: Flux of carbon due to fires (always positive)

concepts.label: Surface_Incident_Longwave_Radiation_MOV
concepts.definition: Surface incident longwave radiation

concepts.label: Above_Ground_Woody_Biomass_MOV
concepts.definition: Total above ground wood biomass

concepts.label: Subsurface_Runoff_MOV
concepts.definition: Gravity soil water drainage and/or soil water lateral flow

concepts.label: Sensible_Heat_MOV
concepts.definition: Sensible heat flux into the boundary layer (positive into atmosphere)

concepts.label: Net_Ecosystem_Exchange_MOV
concepts.definition: Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE=HeteroResp+AutoResp-GPP, positive into atmosphere)

concepts.label: Shortwave_Albedo_MOV
concepts.definition: Shortwave albedo

concepts.label: Surface_Incident_Shortwave_Radiation_MOV
concepts.definition: Surface incident shortwave radiation

concepts.label: Total_Evaporation_MOV
concepts.definition: Sum of all evaporation sources (positive into atmosphere)

concepts.label: Latent_Heat_MOV
concepts.definition: Latent heat flux into the boundary layer (positive into atmosphere)

concepts.label: Field Method
concepts.definition: strawman definition from margaret: a Field_Method is a method for determining a component of primary production that involves observations or measurements of the real world. A field method may have steps which could be considered 'modeling' (such as development of an allometric model of tree growth…

concepts.label: Modeled Method
concepts.definition: strawman definition from Margaret a Modeled_Method (is Simulated_Method better?) uses only data obtained from some source. It does not directly measure any real phenomenon.

concepts.label: Peak Biomass Harvest Method
concepts.definition: Peak_Biomass_Harvest_Method is an estimate of above ground NPP based on the above ground biomass harvested once, usually near the end of the growing season, at or just after the time of peak biomass

concepts.label: Eddy Covariance Method
concepts.definition: The eddy covariance method is an atmospheric measurement technique to measure and calculate vertical turbulent fluxes within atmospheric boundary layers, and analyzes high-frequency wind and scalar atmospheric data series, to yield exchange rates (fluxes) of trace gasses.

concepts.label: Oxygen Evolution LightDark Method
concepts.definition: The stoichiometry of phtotsynthesis is well known. So you can measure O2 evolution, and back calculate to CO2 use. usually, there is a "iight bottle" and "dark bottle". O2 evolution in the Light bottle is the net result, or sum, of all processes (GPP, Autotrophic resp, and probably some…

concepts.label: Allometric Method
concepts.definition: A method determining the relationship between a physical or physiological property of an organism relative to the size of the organism.

concepts.label: LIDAR Method
concepts.definition: A LIDAR_Method for NPP is a methodology to predict the net primary production (NPP) from ground and LiDAR data

concepts.label: MsTMIP_Simulation
concepts.definition: Simulation is the imitation of the operation of a real-world process or system over time. (wikipedia). A MsTMIP Simulation is a simulation carried out by the MsTMIP project (margaret)

concepts.label: Carbon Dioxide Diffusion Flux
concepts.definition: The process by which carbon dioxide in the atmosphere moves across a phase boundary e.g., into the ocean, which is a major sink of atmospheric carbon dioxide. Dissolved carbon dioxide subsequently reacts to form carbonic acid, bicarbonate ions, and carbonate ions, leading to ocean acidification.

concepts.label: Bicarbonate Pool
concepts.definition: The pool of carbon oxoanions resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

concepts.label: Methane Pool
concepts.definition: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is attached by single bonds to four hydrogen atoms. It is a colourless, odourless, non-toxic but flammable gas (b.p. -161degreeC).

concepts.label: Fixed Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: atmospheric carbon dioxide that has been converted into organic carbon compounds, usually by plants and algae via photosynthesis

concepts.label: Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Pool
concepts.definition: Gas phase carbon dioxide molecules in the air surrounding Earth. A principle contributor to climate change and the main source of carbon used by photoautotrophs to store energy during primary production.

concepts.label: Dissolved Carbon Dioxide Pool
concepts.definition: Carbon dioxide that has passed from the gas phase into the dissolved phase, with the the ocean begin the largest component of this pool. This process contributes to acidification by forming carbonic acid with water molecules.

concepts.label: CO2 Enrichment Method
concepts.definition: A method of artificially raising the atmospheric CO2 concentration in field plots in order to study effects on the ecosystem.

concepts.label: Aboveground Net Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: Gross primary productivity (GPP) minus autotrophic respiration (AR) in plant segments other than the roots, e.g. leaves and shoots.

concepts.label: Single-Celled Organism
concepts.definition: An organism that consists of only one cell

concepts.label: Multi-Celled Organism
concepts.definition: An organism that consist of more than one cell

concepts.label: Functional Level
concepts.definition: Functional levels defined here: http://www.physicalgeography.net/fundamentals/9d.html maybe others.

concepts.label: Ecosystem
concepts.definition: Ecosystems are dynamic entities composed of the biological community and the abiotic environment.

concepts.label: Community
concepts.definition: In ecology, a community is an assemblage of two or more populations of different species occupying the same geographical area. (wikipedia) An ecological unit composed of a group of organisms or a population of different species occupying a particular area, usually interacting with each other and…

concepts.label: Population
concepts.definition: A population comprises all the individuals of a given species in a specific area or region at a certain time.

concepts.label: Organism
concepts.definition: An organism is a single individual.

concepts.label: Species
concepts.definition: A group of interbreeding organisms that do not ordinarily breed with members of other groups.

concepts.label: Liquid
concepts.definition: A liquid is a nearly incompressible fluid that conforms to the shape of its container but retains a (nearly) constant volume independent of pressure. As such, it is one of the four fundamental states of matter and is the only state with a definite volume but no fixed shape. A liquid is made up of…

concepts.label: Dissolution Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The rate at which carbon dissolves, moving from one pool to another.

concepts.label: Carbon Dioxide
concepts.definition: A one-carbon compound with formula CO2 in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by organisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food, and taken up…

concepts.label: Carbonate
concepts.definition: Carbon oxoanions that have formula CO3.

concepts.label: Bicarbonate
concepts.definition: Carbon oxoanions resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

concepts.label: Carbon Monoxide
concepts.definition: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is joined only to a single oxygen. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless, toxic gas.

concepts.label: Organic Carbon
concepts.definition: The carbon found in organic molecules.

concepts.label: Organic Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A system that has the capacity to store or release carbon that is either of a biologic origin or can be found or incorporated into a living organism.

concepts.label: Particulate Organic Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A system that has the capacity to store or release carbon, in the form of pieces of plant debris 0.053–2 mm in size.

concepts.label: Inorganic Carbon
concepts.definition: Carbon extracted from ores and minerals and not obtained from plants and living things.

concepts.label: Inorganic Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A component of a system that has the capacity to store or release carbon that is either of a non-biologic origin or cannot be found or incorporated into a living organism. The inorganic carbon species include carbon dioxide, carbonic acid, biocarbonate anion, and carbonate.

concepts.label: Total Living Biomass Carbon Pool
concepts.definition: A fixed carbon pool of the carbon found in living organisms, in a system with the capacity to store and release carbon through process inherent to those organisms.

concepts.label: Tree
concepts.definition: In botany, a tree is a perennial plant with an elongated stem, or trunk, supporting branches and leaves in most species.

concepts.label: Litter Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon in plant litter.

concepts.label: plant-derived organic material
concepts.definition: A portion of organism substance that is or was part of a plant, the whole or part thereof.

concepts.label: phytoplankton
concepts.definition: The autotrophic components of the plankton community and a key factor of oceans, seas and freshwater basin ecosystems. Microscopic, but when present in high enough numbers, some varieties may be produce colored patches on the water surface. From Greek, 'phyto' = plant and 'planktos' = wanderer.

concepts.label: Experiment
concepts.definition: A test under controlled conditions that is made to demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the efficacy of something previously untried.

concepts.label: Manipulative experiment
concepts.definition: Observation of an ecological system of interest under specific, controllable circumstances in an effort to evaluate system response. Fundamentally, manipulative or comarative experments (Hurlbert 1984) require 1) random allocation of treatments (ncluding controls) to experimental units from the…

concepts.label: Natural experiment
concepts.definition: A natural experiment is an empirical study in which individuals (or clusters of individuals) exposed to the experimental and control conditions are determined by nature or by other factors outside the control of the investigators, yet the process governing the exposures arguably resembles random…

concepts.label: Macroalgae
concepts.definition: An operational term for photosynthetic, nonvascular plants that contain chlorophyll a nad have simple reproductive structures, and that are visible to the unaided eye. Includes some members of the red, brown, and green algae, taxonomic groups which do not have a common multicellular ancestor. Some…

concepts.label: diameter
concepts.definition: the length of a straight line passing through the center of a circle and connecting two points on the circumference

concepts.label: circumference
concepts.definition: The circumference (from Latin circumferentia, meaning "carrying around") of a closed curve or circular object is the linear distance around its edge. The circumference of a circle is of special importance in geometry and trigonometry. Informally "circumference" may also refer to the edge itself…

concepts.label: height
concepts.definition: the measurement from base of something to top, or to a fixed point.

concepts.label: concentration_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: Concentration is the abundance of a constituent divided by the total volume of a mixture. The term concentration can be applied to any kind of chemical mixture, but most frequently it refers to solutes and solvents in solutions. Several types of mathematical description can be distinguished: mass…

concepts.label: biomass_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: From Wikipedia: Biomass, in ecology, is the mass of living biological organisms in a given area or ecosystem at a given time. Biomass can refer to species biomass, which is the mass of one or more species, or to community biomass, which is the mass of all species in the community. It can include…

concepts.label: flux_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: the rate of transfer of a substance or energy across a given surface In transport phenomena (heat transfer, mass transfer and fluid dynamics), flux is defined as the rate of flow of a property per unit area, which has the dimensions [quantity]·[time]−1·[area]−1.[Bird et al, 1960] The area is of the…

concepts.label: depth
concepts.definition: the perpendicular measurement downward from a surface

concepts.label: Chlorophyll-a Concentration
concepts.definition: Chlorophyll a is a specific form of chlorophyll used in oxygenic photosynthesis.

concepts.label: Soil Moisture Percentage
concepts.definition: wetness caused by water

concepts.label: temporal_rate_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: A rate measurement is a quantity measured with respect to a second measured quantitiy. In temporal rates, the denominator (second quantity) is time.

concepts.label: Organic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: A concentration of organic carbon in some material.

concepts.label: Freshwater Carbon Dioxide Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon dioxide in fresh water, a naturally occurring chemical compound is composed of a carbon atom covalently double bonded to two oxygen atoms

concepts.label: thickness
concepts.definition: the distance between the top and bottom or front and back surfaces of something

concepts.label: group
concepts.definition: A number of entities taken together as a unit because members share a common characteristic or relation

concepts.label: Near_Surface_Specific_Humidity_MOV
concepts.definition: Near surface specific humidity

concepts.label: carbon dioxide concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon dioxide, a naturally occurring chemical compound is composed of a carbon atom covalently double bonded to two oxygen atoms

concepts.label: Total Soil Carbon
concepts.definition: Soil carbon includes both inorganic carbon as carbonate minerals, and as soil organic matter present in soil

concepts.label: Soil Heterotrophic Respiration Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The respiration rate of heterotrophic organisms (animals and microbes) summed per unit area and time, and occuring in soil.

concepts.label: Grassland Above Ground Net Primary Production Carbon Flux
synonyms: Grassland Above Ground NPP Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: A net primary production measurement which is measured in a grassland and only measures plant segments other than the roots, e.g. leaves and shoots.

concepts.label: Phytoplankton Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The primary production of phytoplankton has been estimated for decades by the 14C (Steemann-Nielsen, 1952) and O2 (Gaarder and Gran, 1927) methods.

concepts.label: Oceanic Total Inorganic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: The total inorganic carbon or dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is the sum of inorganic carbon species in a solution in sea water. The inorganic carbon species include carbon dioxide, carbonic acid, bicarbonate anion, and carbonate.[1] It is customary to express carbon dioxide and carbonic acid…

concepts.label: Carbon Dioxide Flux
concepts.definition: The rate at which a Carbon Dioxide (CO2) moves to or from a particular component of the ecosystem per unit time.

concepts.label: Bicarbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: A carbonate concentration which is comprised of bicarbonate.

concepts.label: Aquatic Inorganic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: A concentration of inorganic carbon occurring in water.

concepts.label: Growth
concepts.definition: The process of increasing in physical size, mass or number, gradually and irreversibly. the process of developing or maturing. the increase in number and spread of small or microscopic organisms. potential synonyms: development, maturation, growing, germination, sprouting; blooming, expansion,…

concepts.label: Tree Height
concepts.definition: Tree height is the vertical distance between the base of the tree and the highest sprig at the top of the tree. The base of the tree is measured for both height and girth as being the elevation at which the pith of the tree intersects the ground surface beneath, or "where the acorn sprouted."

concepts.label: Marine Macroalgae Net Primary Production Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: Gross primary production (GPP) minus autotrophic respiration (AR) by marine macroalgae. Usually expressed per unit area (substrate or water surface) and time. Marine macroalgae occur in oceanic or estuarine environments.

concepts.label: Oceanic Carbon Dioxide Flux
concepts.definition: A flux of carbon across the surface of the ocean, per unit area.

concepts.label: Tree Diameter
concepts.definition: Diameter of a tree. Often measured at a specified, average distance from the ground, eg 4.5 ft (or average person's breast height). May be measured as circumference, then divided by pi.

concepts.label: Tree Circumference
concepts.definition: Distance around the tree, often a specified, average distance from the ground, eg 4.5 ft (or average person's breast height).

concepts.label: Process
concepts.definition: An occurrent that has temporal proper parts and for some time t, p s-depends_on some material entity at t.

concepts.label: Tree growth
concepts.definition: Tree growth is computed from sequential measurements of a tree that often depend on the species and its form. Measurements include (but are not limited to) height, circumference and diamater, eg, diameter at breast height, or DBH.

concepts.label: wet_weight
concepts.definition: The plant, animal, or other material containing the chemical of interest is not dried to remove water. The amount of the chemical found in subsequent analysis is expressed as the weight of chemical divided by the total weight, including any water present, of the material which once contained it.

concepts.label: Tree Diameter at Breast Height
concepts.definition: Domain protocol for measuring the diameter of a tree. Measured at a specified, average distance from the ground, eg 4.5 ft (or average person's breast height). May be measured as circumference, then divided by pi.

concepts.label: ash_free_dry_weight
concepts.definition: Ash-free dry weight is used as an index for percent organic carbon in the quantified substrate.

concepts.label: biomass_density
concepts.definition: Biomass, in ecology, is the mass of living biological organisms in a given area or ecosystem at a given time. Biomass can refer to species biomass, which is the mass of one or more species, or to community biomass, which is the mass of all species in the community. It can include microorganisms,…

concepts.label: biomass_density_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: Biomass, in ecology, is the mass of living biological organisms per unit area at a given time. Biomass can refer to species biomass, which is the mass of one or more species, or to community biomass, which is the mass of all species in the community. It can include microorganisms, plants or animals.

concepts.label: linear_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: A linear measurement assigns a numerical value for the length of an object or between objects. Units of linear measure include inch, foot, meter, kilometer and mile. Linear measurements have one dimension, whereas square measurements have two dimensions and cubic measurements have three.

concepts.label: radius
concepts.definition: A length quality which is equal to the length of any straight line segment that passes from the center of a circle to any endpoint on the circular boundary. The radius is half of the diameter

concepts.label: dry_weight
concepts.definition: the weight of biological material dried at 105 °C until no further water loss takes place. Because water content varies considerably between individuals, dry weight is the most commonly used method of assessing weight in plants and animals.

concepts.label: chlorophyll
concepts.definition: Chlorophyll is a term used for several closely related green pigments found in cyanobacteria and the chloroplasts of algae and plants. Its name is derived from the Greek words chloros ("green") and phyllon ("leaf"). Chlorophyll is an extremely important biomolecule, critical in photosynthesis,…

concepts.label: Carbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbonate, which is a salt of carbonic acid characterized by the presence of the carbonate ion, CO3 2- (one carbon atom, three oxygen atoms negative 2 charge)

concepts.label: Freshwater Carbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbonate, which is a salt of carbonic acid characterized by the presence of the carbonate ion, CO2−3

concepts.label: Freshwater Bicarbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of bicarbonate in freshwater serves a crucial biochemical role in the physiological pH buffering system. Bicarbonate is an intermediate form in the deprotonation of carbonic acid.

concepts.label: Bacteria
concepts.definition: a very large group of microorganisms comprising one of the three domains of living organisms. They are prokaryotic, unicellular, and either free-living in soil or water or parasites of plants or animals See also prokaryote

concepts.label: Algae
concepts.definition: any of numerous groups of chlorophyll-containing, mainly aquatic eukaryotic organisms ranging from microscopic single-celled forms to multicellular forms 100 feet (30 meters) or more long, distinguished from plants by the absence of true roots, stems, and leaves and by a lack of nonreproductive…

concepts.label: dissolved organic carbon
concepts.definition: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is defined as the organic matter that is able to pass through a filter (filters generally range in size between 0.7 and 0.22 um). See particulate organic carbon.

concepts.label: particulate organic carbon
concepts.definition: Particulate organic carbon (POC), or particulate organic matter (POM) is that organic matter suspended in water, and that is not able to pass through a filter (filters generally range in size between 0.7 and 0.22 um). Usually plant or animal origin.

concepts.label: plant
concepts.definition: Defined by the Plant Ontology as a plant structure (PO:0005679) which is a whole organism. PO label is 'whole plant'

concepts.label: soil layer
concepts.definition: A layer which is part of soil. Soil generally consists of visually and texturally distinct layers.

concepts.label: soil active layer
concepts.definition: In environments containing permafrost, the active layer is the top layer of soil that thaws during the summer and freezes again during the autumn.

concepts.label: Soil Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon in soil, which could include all forms (eg, inorganic carbon, carbonate minerals, and as soil organic matter). Soil carbon plays a key role in the carbon cycle, and thus it is important in global climate models.

concepts.label: Aquatic Dissolved Organic Carbon
concepts.definition: Concentration of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) within aquatic systems

concepts.label: Aquatic Particulate Organic Carbon
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon in particulate form that is too large to pass through a filter in aquatic environments

concepts.label: Soil organic matter proportion
concepts.definition: Soil organic content proportion is the fractional amount of all organic matter components of soil, relative to a measurement of the total.

concepts.label: CO2 Concentration in air
synonyms: Near Surface Carbon Dioxide Concentration MOV
concepts.definition: Concentration of CO2 in the earth's atmosphere

concepts.label: Methane Flux
concepts.definition: The rate at which Methane moves to or from a particular component of the ecosystem per unit area, time.

concepts.label: mole fraction
concepts.definition: The number of moles of a component divided by the total number of moles of a solution.

concepts.label: mole fraction of Carbon Dioxide
concepts.definition: A mole fraction measurement with moles of carbon dioxide in the numerator.

concepts.label: carbon monoxide flux
concepts.definition: A carbon flux which is the rate at which carbon monoxide moves to or from a particular component of the ecosystem per unit area and time.

concepts.label: methane concentration
concepts.definition: A carbon compound concentration which consists of methane.

concepts.label: mole fraction of carbon dioxide in air
concepts.definition: A mole fraction of carbon dioxide measurement with the numerator being moles of carbon dioxide and the denominator being the total number of moles of air.

concepts.label: mass fraction
concepts.definition: Ratio of the mass of a substance to the total mass of a mixture. With a denominator of 100, mass fraction can also be expressed as percentage by mass

concepts.label: mass fraction of carbon dioxide
concepts.definition: Ratio of the mass of carbon dioxide to the total mass of a mixture.

concepts.label: mean LI-COR weight fraction of carbon dioxide
synonyms: mean LICOR weight fraction of carbon dioxide
concepts.definition: A mass fraction of carbon dioxide as measured by a LI-COR CO2 analyzer.

concepts.label: molar density
concepts.definition: The volume occupied by a mole of a substance moles/volume

concepts.label: molar density of carbon dioxide
concepts.definition: The volume occupied by a mole of Carbon Dioxide gas.

concepts.label: ratio measurement type
concepts.definition: any contrast of two quantities, one with another-- e.g. to express seeing 222 rabbits per every 10 coyotes, you could use: 222/10 222:10 22.2

concepts.label: dissolved inorganic carbon concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) , which is a broad classification for inorganic molecules of varied origin and composition within aquatic systems. The "dissolved" fraction of inorganic carbon is an operational classification. Many researchers use the term "dissolved" for compounds…

concepts.label: mean weight fraction of carbon dioxide
carbon dioxide partial pressure at sea surface
concepts.definition: A carbon dioxide partial pressure measurement measured at the sea surface.

concepts.label: carbon dioxide partial pressure
concepts.definition: A partial pressure measurement of carbon dioxide gas.

concepts.label: Inorganic carbon concentration
concepts.definition: A concentration of inorganic carbon.

concepts.label: methane partial pressure
concepts.definition: A partial pressure measurement of methane gas.

concepts.label: black carbon concentration
concepts.definition: A carbon concentration which consists of black carbon.

concepts.label: dissolved carbon to dissolved nitrogen ratio
D14C
concepts.definition: The normalized version of d14C.

concepts.label: d13C
concepts.definition: A stable carbon isotope ratio, which is a measure of the ratio of stable isotopes 13C and 12C.

carbon isotope ratio not corrected for Suess effect

electromagnetic radiation
concepts.definition: Electromagnetic radiation is the radiant energy released by certain electromagnetic processes. Visible light is one type of electromagnetic radiation; other familiar forms are invisible to the human eye, such as radio waves, infrared light and X-rays.

concepts.label: proportion_measurementType
concepts.definition: the quotient obtained when the magnitude of a part is divided by the magnitude of the whole, or the ratio obtained in the contrast of two values, where the value of the numerator is added together with that of the contrasting value in the denominator

concepts.label: solar radiation
concepts.definition: Sunlight is a portion of the electromagnetic radiation given off by the Sun, in particular infrared, visible, and ultraviolet light.

concepts.label: temperature_measurementType
concepts.definition: Temperature is measured with thermometers that may be calibrated to a variety of temperature scales. Most scientists measure temperature using the Celsius scale and thermodynamic temperature using the Kelvin scale, which is the Celsius scale offset so that its null point is 0K = −273.15°C, or…

concepts.label: Carbon Flux
concepts.definition: The rate at which a mass or amount of carbon moves to or from a particular component across a surface of the ecosystem per unit time.

concepts.label: Radiative Flux
concepts.definition: Radiative flux is the amount of power radiated through a given area in the form of photons or other elementary particles, typically measured in W/m2. Radiative flux also acts as a generalization of heat flux, which is equal to the radiative flux when restricted to the infrared spectrum. When…

concepts.label: Momentum Flux
concepts.definition: In momentum transfer, the fluid is treated as a continuous distribution of matter. The study of momentum transfer, or fluid mechanics can be divided into two branches: fluid statics (fluids at rest), and fluid dynamics (fluids in motion).

concepts.label: Ash Weight Biomass
concepts.definition: Mass of the ash remaining from combustion of a dried sample, thus the inorganic content.

concepts.label: Nitrogen Fixation Rate
concepts.definition: Nitrogen fixation is a process in which nitrogen (N2) in the atmosphere is converted into ammonia (NH3). Atmospheric nitrogen or molecular dinitrogen (N2) is relatively inert: it does not easily react with other chemicals to form new compounds. The fixation process frees nitrogen atoms from their…

concepts.label: Soil Bulk Density
concepts.definition: Soil bulk density is a property used in reference to mineral components (soil, gravel) defined as the mass of many particles of the material divided by the total volume they occupy.

concepts.label: Belowground Biomass
concepts.definition: The total amount or weight, or energy content, of (a portion of) organisms existing in a specific area at a particular time below a ground surface.

concepts.label: Volumetric Water Content Method
concepts.definition: Water content can be directly measured using a known volume of the material, and a drying oven. Volumetric water content is calculated via the volume of water and the masses of water sample before and after drying in the oven. For materials that change in volume with water content, such as coal,…

concepts.label: High Temperature Combustion
concepts.definition: In a combustion analyzer, half of the sample is injected into a chamber where it is acidified, usually with phosphoric acid, to turn all of the inorganic carbon into carbon dioxide. This is then sent to a detector for measurement. The other half of the sample is injected into a combustion chamber…

concepts.label: biomass
concepts.definition: Biomass is organic matter derived from living, or recently living organisms. Biomass can be used as a source of energy and it most often refers to plants or plant-based materials which are not used for food or feed.

concepts.label: Ammonium Concentration
concepts.definition: Ammonium (NH4) is the form of ammonia (NH3) typically found in water (aquatic environments, soil porewater). It is a postively charged cation. Ammonium is a source of nitrogen for plants, algae and phytoplankton.

concepts.label: area_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: Area is the quantity that expresses the extent of a two-dimensional figure or shape, or planar lamina, in the plane. Surface area is its analog on the two-dimensional surface of a three-dimensional object.

concepts.label: Aquatic Total Organic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of material derived from decaying vegetation, bacterial growth, and metabolic activities of living organisms or chemicals

concepts.label: Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration is the abundance of a constituent divided by the total volume of a mixture. Several types of mathematical description can be distinguished: mass concentration, molar concentration, number concentration, and volume concentration. The term concentration can be applied to any kind of…

concepts.label: Freshwater Total Inorganic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: An aquatic inorganic carbon concentration which is the sum of inorganic carbon species in a solution in freshwater.

concepts.label: Net Assimilation Rate Flux
concepts.definition: the rate of increase of dry weight per unit of leaf area

concepts.label: Dissolved Organic Carbon Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) , which is a broad classification for organic molecules of varied origin and composition within aquatic systems. The "dissolved" fraction of organic carbon is an operational classification. Many researchers use the term "dissolved" for compounds below…

concepts.label: Oceanic Carbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbonate in sea water, which is a salt of carbonic acid characterized by the presence of the carbonate ion, CO2−3

concepts.label: Carbon Percentage
concepts.definition: Proportion of a sample that is carbon, normalized to a denominator of 100.

concepts.label: Carbon Specific Net Production Rate
concepts.definition: A carbon accumulation rate for carbon expressed relative to the amount of carbon originally present.

concepts.label: Net Carbon Respiration Rate Flux
concepts.definition: Carbon respiration (also called carbon emissions and carbon releases) is used in combination with carbon fixation to gauge carbon flux (as CO2) between atmospheric carbon and the global carbon cycle.

concepts.label: Organic Carbon Concentration in Water
concepts.definition: Concentration of total organic carbon (TOC) is the concentration of amount of carbon found in an organic compound

concepts.label: Oceanic Bicarbonate Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of bicarbonate in sea water serves a crucial biochemical role in the physiological pH buffering system. Bicarbonate is an intermediate form in the deprotonation of carbonic acid.

concepts.label: Oceanic Carbon Dioxide Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of carbon dioxide in sea water, a naturally occurring chemical compound is composed of a carbon atom covalently double bonded to two oxygen atoms

concepts.label: Vegetation Carbon Change Percentage
concepts.definition: Change in carbon percentage of vegetation, which are assemblages of plant species and the ground cover they provide.

concepts.label: Soil Carbon Change Percentage
concepts.definition: Soil carbon change percentage includes change of both inorganic carbon as carbonate minerals, and as soil organic matter.

concepts.label: Aboveground Biomass
concepts.definition: The total amount or weight, or energy content, of (a portion of) organisms existing in a specific area at a particular time. In plants, the standing crop pertains to the amount of plant material harvested by normal procedures, and may not necessarily include the entire plant.

concepts.label: Growth Rate
concepts.definition: The rate, or speed, at which the number of organisms in a population increases.

concepts.label: Net Primary Production Biomass Flux
concepts.definition: Net primary production is the synthesis of organic compounds from atmospheric or aqueous carbon dioxide accountig for losses to processes such as cellular respiration. Biomass flux is the change in biomass over a given area over time. It principally occurs through the process of photosynthesis,…

concepts.label: Carbon to Nitrogen Ratio
concepts.definition: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio is a ratio of the mass of carbon to the mass of nitrogen in a substance. It can, amongst other things, be used in analysing sediments and compost. A useful application for C/N ratios is as a proxy for paleoclimate research, having different uses whether the sediment cores…

concepts.label: Wet Weight Biomass
concepts.definition: The biomass is not dried to remove water. The amount of the chemical found in subsequent analysis is expressed as the weight of chemical divided by the total weight, including any water present, of the material which once contained it.

concepts.label: Transpiration Height
concepts.definition: Height of transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers. Water is necessary for plants but only a small amount of water taken up by the roots is used for growth and metabolism.

concepts.label: count_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: Counting is the action of finding the number of elements of a finite set of objects. The traditional way of counting consists of continually increasing a (mental or spoken) counter by a unit for every element of the set, in some order, while marking (or displacing) those elements to avoid visiting…

concepts.label: Stable Carbon Isotope Ratio
concepts.definition: An isotopic signature is a ratio of non-radiogenic 'stable isotopes', stable radiogenic isotopes, or unstable radioactive isotopes of particular elements in an investigated material. The ratios of isotopes in a sample material are measured by isotope ratio mass spectrometry. The atomic mass of…

concepts.label: Carbon Biomass
concepts.definition: Amount of carbon present in biomass

concepts.label: Total Soil Nitrogen Concentration
concepts.definition: total amount of nitrogen (usually mass) per volume of soil

concepts.label: Nitrogen Percentage
concepts.definition: Percentage of a sample that is nitrogen

concepts.label: Plant Material Biomass Density
concepts.definition: Biomass excluding non-plants per unit area at a given time.

concepts.label: Plant Material Biomass
concepts.definition: Biomass excluding non-plants

concepts.label: Non-Plant Material Biomass Density
concepts.definition: Biomass excluding plants per unit area at a given time.

concepts.label: Non-Plant Material Biomass
concepts.definition: Biomass excluding plants

concepts.label: Ash Free Dry Weight Biomass
concepts.definition: The dry mass of a biomass sample or of an object when completely dried (lacks or excluding water).

concepts.label: Sampling Site Area
concepts.definition: a selected subset of a population over the extent of a surface; a sample may be random or nonrandom; representative or nonrepresentative

concepts.label: Dry Weight Biomass
concepts.definition: The weight of dry biomass matter when completely dried (lacks or excluding water).

concepts.label: Leaf Area Index
concepts.definition: Leaf area index (LAI) is a dimensionless quantity that characterizes plant canopies. It is defined as the one-sided green leaf area per unit ground surface area (LAI = leaf area / ground area, m2 / m2) in broadleaf canopies.

concepts.label: Identity
concepts.definition: An identifier is a name that identifies (that is, labels the identity of) either a unique object or a unique class of objects, where the "object" or class may be an idea, physical [countable] object (or class thereof), or physical [noncountable] substance (or class thereof). The abbreviation ID…

concepts.label: Water pH
concepts.definition: pH of water is based on a numeric scale used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution. It is approximately the negative of the logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration, measured in units of moles per liter, of hydrogen ions. More precisely it is the negative of the logarithm…

concepts.label: Count Density
concepts.definition: Number density is an intensive quantity used to describe the degree of concentration of countable objects in a given physical space.

concepts.label: Potential Temperature
concepts.definition: The potential temperature of a parcel of fluid at pressure is the temperature that the parcel would acquire if adiabatically brought to a standard reference pressure, usually 1000 millibars.

concepts.label: Precipitation Rate
concepts.definition: Rate of precipitation, which is any product of the condensation of atmospheric water vapor that falls under gravity.

concepts.label: Air Moisture Percentage
concepts.definition: Water vapor, water vapour or aqueous vapor, is the gaseous phase of water. It is one state of water within the hydrosphere. Water vapor can be produced from the evaporation or boiling of liquid water or from the sublimation of ice. Unlike other forms of water, water vapor is invisible. Under…

concepts.label: Water Salinity
concepts.definition: Salinity is the saltiness or dissolved salt content of a body of water (see also soil salinity). Salinity is an important factor in determining many aspects of the chemistry of natural waters and of biological processes within it, and is a thermodynamic state variable that, along with temperature…

concepts.label: Soil Porewater Salinity Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of soil salinity, the salt content in the soil; the process of increasing the salt content is known as salinization. Salts occur naturally within soils and water. Salination can be caused by natural processes such as mineral weathering or by the gradual withdrawal of an ocean. It can…

concepts.label: Volume Fraction Biomass Concentration
concepts.definition: The density, or more precisely, the volumetric mass density of biomass per unit volume.

concepts.label: areal_density_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: The quantity, amount, weight, etc or things in a given area or space, ie, where the numerator and denominator are different entities. If the numerator and denominator are the same entity, then this would be a measurement of material density (of a 2-dimensional object), eg, as in physics.

concepts.label: Non-Plant Material Count Aerial Density
concepts.definition: Number of non-plant material entities (i.e. animals, fungi) per unit area at a given time

concepts.label: Plant Material Count Aerial Density
concepts.definition: Number of plant material entities (i.e. trees, plant parts) per unit area at a given time

concepts.label: Built Feature Count Aerial Density
concepts.definition: Number of built feature entities (i.e. roads, bridges) per unit area at a given time

concepts.label: Litter Biomass Density
concepts.definition: Mass of undecomposed biomass material found on the forest floor per unit area at a given time.

concepts.label: Tide Height
concepts.definition: Height of tides, which are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun and the rotation of the Earth.

concepts.label: Sea Level Height
concepts.definition: Height of sea level, which is generally used to refer to mean sea level (MSL), an average level for the surface of one or more of Earth's oceans from which heights such as elevations may be measured.

concepts.label: Water Height
concepts.definition: Height of water, which is a transparent fluid which forms the world's streams, lakes, oceans and rain, and is the major constituent of the fluids of organisms.

concepts.label: Wave Height
concepts.definition: The wave height of a surface wave is the difference between the elevations of a crest and a neighbouring trough.

concepts.label: Non-Plant Material Length
concepts.definition: Length of an entity that is not a plant (i.e. body length of a specimen)

concepts.label: Soil Wet Weight
concepts.definition: Soil is not dried to remove water. The amount of the chemical found in subsequent analysis is expressed as the weight of chemical divided by the total weight, including any water present, of the material which once contained it.

concepts.label: Nitrogen Biomass Density
concepts.definition: Mass of nitrogen in biomass per unit area at a given time.

concepts.label: Carbon Biomass Density
concepts.definition: The total mass per area of all carbon in living material in a specific area, habitat, or region.

concepts.label: Time Step
concepts.definition: Interval of time representing duration of observation

concepts.label: Dry Mass Density
concepts.definition: The dry matter of a sample or of an object when completely dried (lacks or excluding water) per area

concepts.label: pressure_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: Pressure is the force applied perpendicular to the surface of an object per unit area over which that force is distributed. Gauge pressure is the pressure relative to the ambient pressure.

concepts.label: Air Pressure
concepts.definition: Atmospheric pressure, sometimes also called barometric pressure, is the pressure exerted by the weight of air in the atmosphere of Earth (or that of another planet). In most circumstances atmospheric pressure is closely approximated by the hydrostatic pressure caused by the weight of air above the…

concepts.label: Seawater Pressure
concepts.definition: Pressure of seawater, or salt water, which is water from a sea or ocean. On average, seawater in the world's oceans has a salinity of about 3.5% (35 g/L, or 599 mM). This means that every kilogram (roughly one litre by volume) of seawater has approximately 35 grams (1.2 oz) of dissolved salts…

concepts.label: Sample Count
concepts.definition: Counting entities within a sample is the action of finding the number of elements of a finite set of entities constrained within a sample.

concepts.label: Entity Count
concepts.definition: Counting entities is the action of finding the number of elements of a finite set of entities.

concepts.label: Aerial Cover Percentage
concepts.definition: The abundances of plant species are often measured by plant cover, i.e. the relative area covered by different plant species in a small plot. Plant cover is not biased by the size and distributions of individuals, and is an important and often measured characteristic of the composition of plant…

concepts.label: Crown Cover Percentage
concepts.definition: Crown cover is the proportion of a stand covered by the crowns of live trees.

concepts.label: Canopy Percentage
concepts.definition: Percentage cover of canopy, which is the aboveground portion of a plant community or crop, formed by the collection of individual plant crowns

concepts.label: Name
concepts.definition: A name is a term used for identification. Names can identify a class or category of things, or a single thing, either uniquely, or within a given context. A personal name identifies, not necessarily uniquely, a specific individual human. The name of a specific entity is sometimes called a proper…

concepts.label: Sampled Individuals Proportion
concepts.definition: A data sample is a set of data collected and/or selected from a statistical population about entities by a defined procedure.

concepts.label: Area Percentage
concepts.definition: An area, such as a quadrat sample, can be used to measure the percentage cover of an entity, such as a certain species

concepts.label: Carbon Specific Gross Production Rate
concepts.definition: A carbon accumulation rate expressed relative to the amount of carbon originally present (e.g, carbon produced per carbon present).

concepts.label: Plant Cover Percentage
concepts.definition: Percentage of plant cover, which is the relative area covered by different plant species in a small plot. Plant cover is not biased by the size and distributions of individuals, and is an important and often measured characteristic of the composition of plant communities.

concepts.label: mass_density_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: The density, or more precisely, the volumetric mass density, of a substance is its mass per unit volume.

concepts.label: volumetric_density_MeasurementType
concepts.definition: The density, or more precisely, the volumetric mass density, of a substance is a characteristic, such as mass or count, per unit volume.

concepts.label: Biomass Volumetric Density
concepts.definition: The density, or more precisely, the volumetric mass density of biomass per unit volume.

concepts.label: Number Volumetric Density
concepts.definition: The density, or more precisely, the volumetric count density of entities per unit volume.

concepts.label: Biomass Concentration
concepts.definition: Abundance of a constituent divided by the total volume of a mixture, or concentration, of biomass, which is organic matter derived from living, or recently living organisms

concepts.label: Water Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of water, which is a transparent fluid which forms the world's streams, lakes, oceans and rain, and is the major constituent of the fluids of organisms.

concepts.label: Seawater Depth
concepts.definition: Depth in a sea, which is a large body of salt water that is surrounded in whole or in part by land.

concepts.label: Snow Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of snow, which is precipitation in the form of flakes of crystalline water ice that falls from clouds

concepts.label: Lake Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of a lake, which is an area of variable size filled with water, localized in a basin, that is surrounded by land, apart from any river or other outlet that serves to feed or drain the lake.

concepts.label: Soil Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of soil, which is a mixture of minerals, organic matter, gases, liquids, and countless organisms that together support life on Earth.

concepts.label: Secchi Depth Method
concepts.definition: The disc is mounted on a pole or line, and lowered slowly down in the water. The depth at which the disk is no longer visible is taken as a measure of the transparency of the water. This measure is known as the Secchi depth and is related to water turbidity.

concepts.label: Litter Depth
concepts.definition: The depth of dead plant material, such as leaves, bark, needles, and twigs, that have fallen to the ground. This detritus or dead organic material and its constituent nutrients are added to the top layer of soil, commonly known as the litter layer or O horizon ("O" for "organic").

concepts.label: Soil Active Layer Depth
concepts.definition: In environments containing permafrost, the active layer is the top layer of soil that thaws during the summer and freezes again during the autumn. In all climates, whether they contain permafrost or not, the temperature in the lower levels of the soil will remain more stable than that at the…

concepts.label: Specific Net Production Flux
concepts.definition: Net primary production (NPP) flux that relative to another mass (or other measurement of amount, eg, leaf area, plant wet weight) that primary producers create in a given length of time over a given area Net primary production flux is the rate at which all the plants in an ecosystem produce net…

concepts.label: Stream Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of a stream, which is a body of water with a current, confined within a bed and banks.

concepts.label: Groundwater Depth
concepts.definition: Depth of groundwater (or ground water), which is the water present beneath Earth's surface in soil pore spaces and in the fractures of rock formations. A unit of rock or an unconsolidated deposit is called an aquifer when it can yield a usable quantity of water. The depth at which soil pore spaces…

concepts.label: Tree Crown Diameter
concepts.definition: Diameter of the crown of a tree, which consists of the mass of foliage and branches growing outward from the trunk of the tree. The average crown spread is the average horizontal width of the crown, taken from dripline to dripline as one moves around the crown.

concepts.label: Tree Canopy Diameter
concepts.definition: Diameter of the canopy, which is the aboveground portion of a plant community or crop, formed by the collection of individual plant crowns

concepts.label: Ground Heat Flux
concepts.definition: Ground heat flux is the process where heat energy is transferred from the Earth’s surface to the subsurface of the Earth via conduction. It is an important component of the Earth’s surface energy budget. Ground heat flux can be presented by the amount of heat transmitted per unit of area per unit…

concepts.label: Tag Number
concepts.definition: A tag number provides an alphanumeric string of characters to refer to an entity. A TagNumber is typically used to uniquely identify an entity such as a sample or an individual specimen such as a tree or a rock sample.

concepts.label: Latent Heat Flux
concepts.definition: Latent heat flux is the flux of heat from the Earth's surface to the atmosphere that is associated with evaporation of water at the surface and subsequent condensation of water vapor in the troposphere. It is an important component of Earth's surface energy budget. Latent heat flux is commonly…

concepts.label: Tree Canopy Height
concepts.definition: Height of the canopy, which is the aboveground portion of a plant community or crop, formed by the collection of individual plant crowns

concepts.label: Tree Crown Height
concepts.definition: Height of the crown of a tree, which consists of the mass of foliage and branches growing outward from the trunk of the tree. The average crown spread is the average horizontal width of the crown, taken from dripline to dripline as one moves around the crown.

concepts.label: Plant Material Height
concepts.definition: Height of a physical entity that is a plant or part of a plant (i.e. tree trunk height)

concepts.label: Precipitation Height
concepts.definition: Height of precipitation, which is any product of the condensation of atmospheric water vapor that falls under gravity. The main forms of precipitation include drizzle, rain, sleet, snow, graupel and hail. Precipitation occurs when a portion of the atmosphere becomes saturated with water vapor, so…

concepts.label: Carbon Dioxide Pressure
concepts.definition: Pressure of carbon dioxide gas, which is composed of a carbon atom covalently double bonded to two oxygen atoms.

concepts.label: Air Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of air

concepts.label: Seawater Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of water in sea

concepts.label: Water Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of water

concepts.label: Peat Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of peat

concepts.label: Ground Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of ground

concepts.label: Soil Temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of soil

concepts.label: lake water temperature
concepts.definition: Objective comparative measure of hot or cold of water in lake

concepts.label: Specific Gross Production Flux
concepts.definition: Gross primary production (GPP) flux that relative to another mass (or other measurement of amount, eg, leaf area, plant wet weight) that primary producers create in a given length of time over a given area

concepts.label: Wind Speed
concepts.definition: The speed of wind is the rate of change of its position with respect to a frame of reference, and is a function of time.

concepts.label: Water Velocity
concepts.definition: The velocity of water is the rate of change of its position with respect to a frame of reference, and is a function of time.

concepts.label: Seawater Velocity
concepts.definition: The velocity of sea water is the rate of change of its position with respect to a frame of reference, and is a function of time.

concepts.label: volume_measurementType
concepts.definition: Volume is the quantity of three-dimensional space enclosed by a closed surface, for example, the space that a substance (solid, liquid, gas, or plasma) or shape occupies or contains.

concepts.label: Precipitation Volume
concepts.definition: Volume of precipitation, which is any product of the condensation of atmospheric water vapor that falls under gravity

concepts.label: Physical Feature Width
concepts.definition: Width of a physical abiotic entity (i.e. width of a stream)

concepts.label: Soil Dry Weight
concepts.definition: Weight of soil dried at 105 °C until no further water loss takes place

concepts.label: mass_measurementType
concepts.definition: mass is a property of a physical body. It is a measure of an object's resistance to acceleration (a change in its state of motion) when a force is applied. It also determines the strength of its mutual gravitational attraction to other bodies. In the theory of relativity a related concept is the…

concepts.label: Chlorophyll Concentration
concepts.definition: Adapted from http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyll

concepts.label: Oxygen Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of oxygen, which is a chemical element that is a member of the chalcogen group on the periodic table and is a highly reactive nonmetal and oxidizing agent that readily forms oxides with most elements as well as other compounds

concepts.label: Pheophytin Concentration
concepts.definition: Concentration of pheophytin, which is chemical compound that serves as the first electron carrier intermediate in the electron transfer pathway of photosystem II (PS II) in plants, and the photosynthetic reaction center (RC P870) found in purple bacteria

concepts.label: Specific Flux
concepts.definition: Flux where the units of the numerator include mass and units of the denominator include mass (or some other measurement of 'amount', eg leaf area) in addition to flux units of area and time

concepts.label: Specific Respiration Flux
concepts.definition: Ecosystem respiration flux is the respiration occurring by the living organisms in a specific ecosystem over a given area, relative to some other measure of those organisms.

concepts.label: chromophoric dissolved organic matter absorbance
concepts.definition: An absorbance measurement of the optically measurable component of dissolved organic matter in water.

concepts.label: chromophoric dissolved organic matter absorbance ratio
synonyms: colored dissolved organic matter absorbance ratio

concepts.label: specific ultraviolet absorbance
concepts.definition: An absorbance measurement type which is the absorbance of ultraviolet light in a water sample at a specified wavelength normalized for a dissolved organic carbon concentration.
